telemetry.rationale: One-second real host counter cadence, five-minute warmup plus five-second margin; retain existing 95% coverage and two-second gap/freshness gates. Exact bounds/available frontier and actual submission freshness are independently checked. No normalized demand assumed.

configuration_rationale: Larger real five-minute three-window collection, all source arrivals from audited training-only day-index selection retained at original spacing. Three arms matched within each actual source window; rotated order balances arm positions across source windows without outcome search. Initial table/data/client/SQL conditions unchanged. Now is horizon start, later midpoint150seconds: explicit intervention, not a hardcoded learned policy. Five-minute horizon equals longest existing telemetry history and allows several measured rewrite durations to observe resulting layout consequences; operational18:30IST cutoff never cancels active work. One arm/window, three demand profiles, no power/independent-calibration claim or fitting. No pooled causal winner or synthetic targets.
limitations: One episode/arm/window across three source windows is engineering completeness and demand variation screening, not statistical power, independent conformal calibration or accepted cost training.
One warehouse with three five-minute training windows, imposed benchmark mix and controlled SF1 fragmentation; no production SQL, ingestion or scale claim.
Rotated order balances arm positions but does not eliminate cache/time trends or shared-host dependence.
Equal logical content and file row/byte signature do not establish identical cache state or all physical locality.
Actual metadata/refresh/state-publication overhead and generator jitter measured; controller snapshot may lag commit.
Common-horizon residual queue and maintenance completion recorded separately; no arbitrary scalar weight or invented SLA.
No adaptive forecaster, trained cost model, oracle input, optimized deferral or scheduling benefit claim.
